info.title: larql-server
info.description: HTTP API for vindex knowledge queries, inference, and remote MoE expert shards.

post.description:
JSON request: `{"token_ids": [...]}`.
Binary request (`Content-Type: application/x-larql-ffn`):
  - 4 bytes: num_tokens (u32 LE)
  - num_tokens × 4 bytes: token_ids (u32 LE)

JSON response: `{"residual": [[f32, ...], ...], "seq_len": N, ...}`.
Binary response: seq_len×hidden_size f32 LE, prefixed by two u32 headers.

requestBody.description: JSON `{token_ids: [u32]}` OR binary `application/x-larql-ffn`: `[num_tokens u32 LE][token_ids u32 LE...]`.

200.description: Binary response when the request used `Content-Type: application/x-larql-ffn`: `[seq_len u32][hidden u32][seq_len × hidden f32 LE]`.

get.description:
Returns the scaled f32 embedding vector for a single token ID.
The key (token_id) is a 32-bit integer; the value is a deterministic
function of the model weights — so the response is immutably cacheable:

  Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

CDN-friendly: a reverse proxy or browser can cache the embedding for
any token permanently, eliminating repeated lookups for high-frequency
tokens (the, a, in, …) on the decode path.

Response (binary, 10 KB for hidden=2560):
  [f32 × hidden_size] — LE bytes, pre-scaled

Response (JSON, if Accept: application/json):
  {"token_id": N, "embedding": [f32, ...], "hidden_size": N}

200.description: Mean-pooled embeddings (not contrastively trained — use at your own risk).

requestBody.description: JSON `{requests:[{layer, expert_id, residual}]}` OR binary `application/x-larql-expert` wire (see docs/server-spec.md).

200.description: Expert ownership range for this shard

requestBody.description: Binary wire: one pre-norm residual + K (expert_id, weight) pairs for a single layer. Router-weighted sum is returned as f32. See `docs/server-spec.md` for the exact packed layout.
Same shape as `/v1/experts/layer-batch` but residual is f16 to cut upload bandwidth by 2×.
N packed layer tasks — each `(layer, residual, expert_ids, weights)`. Server runs every task in parallel via rayon and returns N per-layer f32 outputs in one response.

200.description: N per-layer f32 outputs, one per task

post.summary:
Q8K-prenormed variant: client pre-quantises h_norm, server skips
`pre_experts_norm` and `quantize_h_norm_for_q4k` — just the matvec.
4× smaller upload; response is standard f32.

requestBody.description: Same shape as `/v1/experts/multi-layer-batch` but the client has already applied `pre_experts_norm` and quantised `h_norm` to Q8K, saving ~4× upload bandwidth. Response is standard f32.

200.description: N per-layer f32 outputs, one per task

post.description:
Accepts JSON (`{"residual": [...], "top_k": 5, "temperature": 1.0}`) or

requestBody.description: JSON `{residual: [f32; hidden_size], top_k, temperature}` OR binary `application/x-larql-ffn` with raw hidden_size f32 LE bytes.

101.description:
WebSocket upgrade. After upgrade:

**Client → server** (text frames, JSON):
- `{"type":"describe", "entity":"France", "band":"all"}` — streams layer-by-layer describe.
- `{"type":"infer", "prompt":"The capital of France is", "top":5, "mode":"walk"}` — streams top-K predictions one at a time.

**Server → client** (text frames, JSON):
- `{"type":"layer", "layer":N, "edges":[...]}` — per-layer describe output.
- `{"type":"done", "entity":..., "total_edges":N, "latency_ms":M}` — describe finished.
- `{"type":"prediction", "rank":I, "token":..., "probability":P}` — inference result.
- `{"type":"infer_done", "prompt":..., "mode":..., "predictions":N, "latency_ms":M}` — inference finished.
- `{"type":"error", "message":...}` — protocol or runtime error.

requestBody.description: Dense-FFN walk. Accepts JSON `WalkFfnRequest` (Content-Type `application/json`) OR the packed binary wire (requires `full_output = true`): Content-Type `application/x-larql-ffn[-f16|-i8]` declares the INBOUND residual encoding, independently of the `Accept`-negotiated response format. See `docs/server-spec.md` for the full wire layout.

requestBody.description: Q8K-prenormed dense-FFN batch: client has applied FFN input norm + Q8 quantisation. 404 if the vindex lacks interleaved Q4K data.

ApplyPatchBody.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/patches/apply`. Provide either a `url`
pointing at a `.vlp` file (local path or `hf://` URL) or an
inline `patch` object. One of the two is required.

url.description: Local path, `http(s)://`, or `hf://` URL to a `.vlp` patch file.

patch.description:
Inline patch payload. See VindexPatch docs for schema; includes
`description`, `base_model`, and `operations` (INSERT / DELETE).

CapabilitiesResponse.description:
`GET /v1/capabilities`. The `sources` / `explorer` /
`runtime` blocks are generated from
`crate::capabilities::ROUTE_CAPABILITIES` and the mounted-route
ledger, so this schema documents the *shape*; the authority for
which keys appear is that table, not this struct.

schema.description:
Report schema version. A client that does not recognise it
must refuse the document rather than read the keys it knows.

sources.description: Which source reference forms each source-taking verb accepts.

explorer.description: The read surface over a bound container.

runtime.description: What this process will do with the bound model, and on what.

routes.description: Every path this server mounted, sorted.

relation.description: Relation label (present when a probe-confirmed label exists).

ErrorBody.description: JSON body returned for every error response.

path.description:
Filesystem path to a VINDEX2 or VINDEX3 container — the same
path `--vindex-path` already accepts. No registry/name
resolution yet (`docs/runtime-lifecycle-design.md`'s explicit
non-goals for this rung).

residual.description: Flat f32 residual of length hidden_size (one position, post-all-layers).

ModelEntry.description: One entry in the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models` list.

path.description: Route prefix for this model. `/v1/{id}` in multi-model mode, `/v1` otherwise.

OpenAIErrorBody.description: Top-level OpenAI error envelope: `{"error": {message, type, param, code}}`.

OpenAIErrorPayload.description:
Wire shape for the `error` field. Always includes `param` and `code`
even when null — some SDKs hard-key on those keys.

Public so the OpenAPI schema for 4xx/5xx responses on the OpenAI
endpoints can reference it.

OpenAiChatRequest.description:
OpenAI `POST /v1/chat/completions` request. `messages` is an array
of `{role: "system"|"user"|"assistant"|"tool", content, ...}`; tools
and structured output are open JSON (see OpenAI docs).

embedding.description: `[f32]` when `encoding_format = "float"`, or a base64 string otherwise.

OpenAiEmbeddingsRequest.description: Subset of the OpenAI `POST /v1/embeddings` request body.

model.description: Model id. Required in multi-model mode; ignored otherwise.

input.description: String, string[], int[] (single sequence), or int[][] (batch of sequences).

dimensions.description: Requested output dimensionality (ignored; returns native hidden size).

OpenAiResponsesRequest.description:
OpenAI `POST /v1/responses` request. `input` is a string or an
array of input items (`message`, `function_call`,
`function_call_output`); tools use the flattened Responses shape.

input.description: String, or array of input items.

store.description:
Persist for `previous_response_id` chaining (default true;
in-memory and bounded).

tools.description: Function tools, Responses shape: `[{type, name, description, parameters}]`.

sources.description:
The artifacts to plan, as `hf://owner/repo[@revision]` or —
where the profile permits it — local checkpoint paths.

A list, not a string, because a VINDEX3 plan is a *system*
plan: several artifacts can compose into one model, and their
interfaces are part of the verdict. One source is the ordinary
case and is written `["hf://owner/repo"]`. There is deliberately
no singular `source` alias — two spellings of one request is a
second thing to keep in agreement.

metal_compiled.description:
Whether this binary was compiled with Metal-accelerated MoE
expert dispatch — a compile-time fact, not a claim that
Metal is driving the current request.

resident_bytes.description:
Peak resident-set size of this process (`getrusage`), in
bytes. `None` on a non-Unix target or a syscall failure.

model_bytes.description:
Estimated resident footprint of the bound model's weights.
`None` when no model is bound, or on a VINDEX3 container
(no estimator exists yet).

quantization.description:
`None` for a VINDEX3 container — it carries no single
top-level quant tag the way a VINDEX2 `index.json` does.

prefill_tokens_per_second.description: `None` until at least one generation has completed.

RuntimeResponse.description:
`GET /v1/runtime` — server + model + backend + memory +
performance snapshot. Never constructed at runtime (the handler
builds `serde_json::Value` directly); this exists purely so the
OpenAPI spec documents the shape.

available.description:
Whether a resident KV state owned by this session can be
resumed from.

input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens already absorbed into the resident state(s).

resumptions.description: Generations on this session where resumption engaged.

reused_tokens_total.description: Prompt tokens served from resumed KV, cumulative.

deleted.description:
False when the session was already gone — deletion is
idempotent, not an error.

data.description: Live sessions, most recently used first.

active.description: How many patches are applied to this session.

ids.description:
Patch identities, in application order. Contents are not
exposed here — `/v1/patches` is the authority for those.

model.description: Runtime binding the session was created against.

expires_at.description: When the session expires if left idle from `last_used_at`.

state.description:
Lifecycle state; `active` is the only observable value —
expired sessions are absent, not listed.

server.description:
Server-level counters: uptime, request count, and the
bounded per-client stores (patch sessions, stored
responses, V3 KV continuation cache with hit/miss counts).

num_experts.description: Total number of experts in the model (0 for non-MoE models).

owned_start.description: First expert ID owned by this shard (inclusive).

owned_end.description: Last expert ID owned by this shard (inclusive).

layers.description:
Specific layers to prefetch (`madvise WILLNEED`). Defaults to
every owned layer when omitted — the typical case for boot
warmup.

skip_weights.description:
Skip the inference-weight load. Use when the server was started
with `--no-infer` and you only want mmap prefetch, not
`lm_head` / `norms` / gate-f32 expansion.

warmup_hnsw.description:
Eager-build HNSW for every owned layer (mirrors the existing
`--warmup-hnsw` boot flag, exposed here so operators can warm
a running server without restarting). Requires HNSW already
enabled via `--hnsw`.

experts_prefetched.description:
Number of (layer, expert) pairs whose pages were read into the page cache.
Zero for non-MoE models or when `skip_weights = true`.
